---
title: "International Finance"
subtitle: "Kedge Business School · IBBA · 2026"
---

This course builds a set of operational models of how international financial
markets work — and then spends most of its time on where they break.
Informational efficiency, financial crises, regulation, behavioural finance,
mostly through papers rather than through me talking. A second objective, and I
mean it: what a more responsible practice of finance would look like after 2008.

::: {.note}
**No textbook.** Reference: Mishkin, F.S. & Eakins, S.G. (2008), *Financial
Markets and Institutions*, 7th ed., Pearson.
Course description and grades are on [LEARN](http://learn.kedgebs.com).
:::

## Readings

Read the paper **before** the session it belongs to. We discuss it; I do not
summarise it for you.

| Sessions | Reading |
|:--|:---|
| 1–2 | Monasterolo, I. (2020), *Climate Change and the Financial System*, **Annual Review of Resource Economics** 12 |
| 3–4 | Sartzetakis, E.S. (2021), *Green bonds as an instrument to finance low carbon transition*, **Economic Change and Restructuring** 54 |
| 5–6 | Muñoz, F. (2020), *How do the size and independence of the board of trustees affect the financial and sustainable performance of socially responsible mutual funds?*, **Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management** 27(4) |

## Assessment

| | Weight | When | Conditions |
|:---|:--:|:---|:---|
| Individual assignment | 20% | Session 7 | 20 minutes, no documents |
| Group work — security analysis | 40% | Session 8 | Groups of five, 12-minute presentation |
| Final examination | 40% | Session 10 | Individual, written, documents allowed |

**A calculator is required for most sessions.** Not your phone.

### The group work

Five students per group, twelve minutes. Pick one security and answer four
questions about it:

1. What are the **characteristics** of the security?
2. What are the **actual and expected situations** in that market?
3. What is the **international dimension** of it?
4. What are the **risks and opportunities**?

Choose something you can find real data on. Groups that pick an exotic
derivative spend the whole presentation explaining the instrument and never
reach questions 2 to 4.
